subject: INLA crashes with high-dimensional large data

messages.author: 2a3b73736ea89ff6
messages.subject: INLA crashes with high-dimensional large data
parts:
Hi INLA team,

I have a poisson model with random spatial effect (nngp implemented with rgeneric), and I tried the model with some simulated data. The model performs well even with ~2 million observations in 20,000 locations (many replicates at each location) and 13 covariates (all randomly generated from bernoulli distribution). However, the inla model crashed after 1-2 hours computation when I increase the number of covariates to 30. I am running the models using a linux server with 4 CPU cores and ~120 G RAM. During the process, the Mem usage is about 15-20% by monitoring the -top of the server. Since the Mem usage is low and only one core is used, I am assuming this is not caused by the hardware? Can anyone help me solve this? Thanks.

My code is like:
inla.setOption( num.threads = 1 )

f.nngp<-nclaims~ -1 + intercept + cov1 + cov2+ cov3 + cov4+ cov5 + cov6+ cov7 + cov8 

  + cov9 + cov10+ cov11 + cov12+ cov13  + cov14+ cov15 + cov16+ cov17 + cov18 

  + cov19 + cov20+cov21 + cov22+ cov23  + cov24+ cov25 + cov26+ cov27 + cov28 

  + cov29 + cov30+f(idx,model = nngp.model)

 

m.nngp<-inla(f.nngp, data = data.frame(intercept=1,train), family="poisson", control.compute = list(dic=TRUE,waic=TRUE,config=FALSE),

   control.inla=list(int.strategy="eb",strategy="gaussian"),

             verbose=TRUE)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crashes with high-dimensional large data
parts:
For this you need to use the PARDISO library, see

inla.pardiso()

and a recent testing version of the INLA. Make sure to follow the
optimization suggestion in the vignette, avoid to replicate computations
and cache in the function's environment.

libR run serial only, by design, and we cannot run more than one in
parallel.

let me know how this goes. the next alternative is for me to run it
here, then I need code.

Best
H
